chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the Muslim kills the Christian, and the family of the Christian intend to kill him, they can kill him and pay the excess of what is between the two blood-money amounts.

key_terms.الدِّيَتَيْنِ: The two blood-money amounts (diya of the Muslim and diya of the Christian)
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيَّ: The Christian (specifically a Zimmi/non-Muslim subject in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on retaliation when a Muslim kills a Christian and the Christian's family kills the Muslim in return?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'qisas' (retaliation) in interfaith homicide, specifically addressing the scenario where a Christian family chooses execution over financial compensation. It establishes that the 'fadl' (excess value) of the Muslim's blood money is absorbed by the act of killing, meaning the Christian heirs pay no additional difference, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the valuation of life in retributive justice. This ruling highlights the practical application of diya disparities in the context of the dhimmi status within early Islamic society.
